speaker: george_bryan
text: He has a clerk. I have business near the courts. You have lungs that have just come clear of a cold. Stand, and hear how a trouble is made small enough to carry.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I will stand. I am not here to be heard. The play is at two, and it is not mine.

speaker: (the clerk)
text: The short of it is a ditch, a hedge, and three acres. I have put that on a sheet. The sheet is two shillings.

speaker: (the client)
text: The ditch was mine before the hedge was his. The three acres take their water from my side. Your sheet has the hedge. It does not have the milk.

speaker: (the clerk)
text: The milk will not fit on the sheet the court can carry. I have charged you for the short of it.

speaker: (the client)
text: The milk was lost when his steward walked the bank, in the Armada year. I will not lose it a second time because your sheet is tired.

speaker: george_bryan
text: He paid to have it shortened. Hear what he does with the paying.

speaker: (the client)
text: Then I will say it at the length it has. Write the milk back in. Write the steward. Write that the hedge drinks from my ditch. I have been charged for the short, and I am paying the time to have the long of it said in this hall.

speaker: (the clerk)
text: Two shillings was the short. The long is the same sheet with his words put back on it. He may have them. I do not add a second fee for a man who will not stop.

speaker: (the client)
text: Put them back, then. I will hear every word before I go. A sheet that forgets the milk is a sheet about another man's field.

speaker: george_bryan
text: There. Greater length, after the charge for the shortening. I have seen this shape all morning, and this one has a ditch in it, which makes it easier to follow.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I have heard him. I have nothing to put on his sheet. The milk is his, and the two shillings are his, and neither of them is a line of mine.

speaker: (the clerk)
text: The sheet will do. Next.

speaker: (the client)
text: It will do when I have heard the milk in it. Not before. You will read it back.

speaker: george_bryan
text: Come away while he has him read it back. The Hall can spare two men who are not in the suit. Two Gents is at two. You are not cast. I would not have you late for a play you are only standing at.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I am not cast. I will be in the parlour door, if I am in the house at all. The Rose has The Wise Man. I am not going there.

speaker: (the clerk)
text: Read it back, then. Ditch, hedge, three acres, and the milk, since you will not leave without the milk. The steward walked the bank. The hedge drinks from your ditch. Two shillings, and the sheet is as long as you have made it.

speaker: (the client)
text: That is the long of it. That is what I paid the short to become. I will hear it once more, and then I will be a man with a sheet instead of a field.

speaker: george_bryan
text: Once more is how a hall earns its morning. You have heard the shape. You do not need the second reading of the milk.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I have the shape. A man charged for the short of a thing, saying the long of it anyway. I am not here to rent him a better sentence.

speaker: (the client)
text: I do not want a better sentence. I want the milk on the sheet, in words a clerk will not be ashamed to read. You, in the plain coat. You are not my lawyer. Do not become one. Lawyers are dearer than two shillings.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I am not your lawyer. I write for a yard, not for a court. Your two shillings are safer without me.

speaker: george_bryan
text: Which is why we are leaving. Hilary term can open without an audience of players. We have stretched the lungs. The caps will still be here after dinner, and we will not.

speaker: (the clerk)
text: Next. And take your sheet, sir, before you invent a second steward.

speaker: george_bryan
text: Then the door is far enough. We have stood. The lungs have had their stretch. Leave him his milk.
